_premise: A showcase for a design skill is judged by whether it survives its own critique. This one presents every claim as a labelled specimen on a bench: two arms, same brief, measured, annotated. The comparison is the visual identity.
_note: Authored in OKLCH (see design/palette.py, which round-trips through scripts/color.py). Hex below is the exact sRGB round-trip, for tooling only. Every text pair is contrast-verified; the verification is a build step, not a claim.

_type.display: Instrument Serif — the argument. Thesis lines and plate titles only.
_type.ui: Geist — the interface. Navigation, prose, controls.
_type.mono: Geist Mono — the evidence. Labels, plate numbers, measurements, code, tokens.
_type._why: Three kinds of content live here — an argument, an interface, and evidence — so there are three faces and each one owns exactly one of them. A reader can tell what kind of thing they are looking at without reading it.
_type.scale_ratio: 1.2 for UI (dense technical), with a deliberate break to editorial sizes for display

_shape._why: A specimen card and a lab plate have square corners. 2px is a printing tolerance, not a style. It also makes the build visibly not-shadcn-default, which for this subject is load-bearing.

_elevation._why: A drop shadow on one pane of a two-pane comparison adds visual weight to that pane. The instrument must not put its thumb on the scale.

_motion.the_one_moment: the comparison slider — it tracks the pointer 1:1 with no easing, because a lagging divider makes the two arms look misaligned when they are not
_motion.never_animates: page entry, section reveal on scroll, anything that repeats on every scroll
